items.title: Suno Studio 2.0 puts an AI assistant in the DAW
items.excerpt: Suno's Studio 2.0 adds a chat-style AI assistant you can direct 'like any other member of the band', alongside MIDI editing, stem separation and automation curves. It pushes the AI song generator further into real DAW territory.

items.title: Suno launches Studio 2.0 with MIDI support, an AI chat bar… and no download limit
items.excerpt: Suno's revamped Studio adds MIDI import/record/edit on the timeline, third-party plugin support and an AI chat bar, with downloads from Studio sessions exempt from the new library caps. Suno frames it as a pro workstation rather than a prompt box.

items.title: Beatport is banning fully AI-generated tracks
items.excerpt: Beatport will refuse tracks 'wholly or substantially' generated by AI while still allowing AI-assisted production where humans keep creative control. The store cites a survey where 77% of DJs backed human artists.

items.title: Beatport Confirms AI Ban Under Bolstered Beatdapp Partnership
items.excerpt: Beyond banning fully machine-made audio, Beatport will tag AI-assisted uploads using expanded Beatdapp detection. Producers releasing with AI in the chain now face disclosure at the store level.

items.title: Beatport bars tracks 'wholly or substantially generated by AI'
items.excerpt: Beatport joins Bandcamp in outright refusing fully AI-made music, drawing the line at 'substantial' human authorship. The policy shows dance-music storefronts converging on disclosure-plus-ban rules.

items.title: Spotify finally get tough on AI slop as platform adds 'Persona Badge' to mark out AI-generated 'artists'
items.excerpt: Spotify will badge artist profiles that don't represent a real person and pull them from default recommendations. The label targets fake identities rather than AI-assisted production methods.

items.title: Spotify Labels AI Artists With 'AI Persona' Tag and Cuts Them From Recommendations
items.excerpt: The AI Persona label rolls out mid-September and removes flagged profiles from editorial and algorithmic recommendations, though royalties are untouched. Self-declaration plus manual review decides who gets tagged.

items.title: Spotify to start labelling 'AI personas'
items.excerpt: Spotify asks artists to self-declare AI personas and will apply badges from next month, with an appeals process for disputed profiles. It is the clearest streaming-side rulebook yet for AI-fronted acts.

items.title: Daft Punk's Thomas Bangalter explains why he's 'not interested in the creative use of AI'
items.excerpt: Bangalter argues that unpredictability is the point of creative work and that generative tools optimise it away. A pointed counterweight from an artist whose career was built on machines.

items.title: After Universal and Merlin deals, Spotify inks agreement with Kobalt for AI-powered 'fan-made' covers and remixes
items.excerpt: Kobalt is the first publisher outside UMG to license Spotify's forthcoming AI remix and cover tool. The deal clears publishing rights for listener-made derivative versions inside the app.

items.title: IK Multimedia just totally revamped its Tonex Player and made its tone ecosystem a lot easier to use
items.excerpt: Tonex 2.0 Player enters public beta with 220 new Premium V2 neural Tone Models and a redesigned capture-to-stage workflow. Neural amp modelling keeps moving from novelty to default guitar rig.

items.title: Brian May asked AI to recreate the cover of Queen's The Game. He wasn't happy with the results
items.excerpt: May ran a generative image test on one of rock's best-known album covers and found the result badly wrong. A blunt artist-side reality check on generative art fidelity.

items.title: Suno Vinyl: Press Your AI-Generated Music to Vinyl
items.excerpt: Suno opened a waitlist for pressing generated tracks to a 12-inch record with a custom sleeve, from $45 plus shipping. The pitch turns prompt output into an object.

items.title: Music to confuse AI might be the next new genre
items.excerpt: Musicians are deliberately uploading strange, degraded tracks to poison AI training sets, turning data resistance into an aesthetic. CDM traces projects making dataset sabotage a creative practice.

items.title: Immanent Audio releases IA De-Esser, a FREE de-essing plugin
items.excerpt: A free four-slot de-esser for macOS and Windows, whose developer says AI sped up development while insisting on shipping no code they don't understand. A small, concrete look at AI inside plugin building.

items.title: KOMCA Retools AI Policy to Allow Machine-Assisted Copyrights
items.excerpt: South Korea's KOMCA reversed its blanket no-AI stance and will now register AI-assisted works. Korean songwriters using generative tools regain a registration path.

items.title: Tyga Admits to Using Suno For Latest Album — Is It Chart Ineligible?
items.excerpt: Tyga openly says Suno was used to make his new album, testing the IFPI's fresh chart-eligibility rules for generative AI. A mainstream artist workflow disclosure with immediate industry consequences.
